scope: Theorem 8.16 (Numerical exclusion) of the manuscript “Purely cosmetic surgery on knots in the three-sphere” (preprints/Purely-Cosmetic-Surgery-on-Knots-in-the-Three-Sphere-September-23-2026/paper.pdf), one of the manuscripts of result family 306 of openai/math at commit 1581d4cbdd69. The statement is quoted verbatim from the text that pdftotext 24.02.0 (-raw -enc UTF-8) extracts from the PDF (SHA-256 ee916c92b825a868), with whitespace normalised, and was found there under this heading on PDF page 106. Text extraction flattens typeset mathematics (superscripts, subscripts, fractions, large operators, delimiters), so the quote can read differently from the typeset statement and can carry characters with no Unicode meaning; the PDF is authoritative. Finding the quote shows that the manuscript states it, not that it is true. AMVO has checked nothing about this claim.
statement: Choose the old-cap data, outside delays, exceptional evalu- ations, finite stack, metric sizes, and sufficiently small equation data in the order of Lemma 8.12 and Corollary 7.10, with ntot D > 0. Assume the regularity, incidence, and projection properties of Definition 8.7. Then the only fixed-type tuples meeting the nonphase cuts are the legitimate unbro- ken isolated type A instantons. The free part after the η = ntot D − 1 phase cuts and phase quotient has expected dimension one. Its only possible true-face or positive-loss limiting tuples are single trace-minimum lens faces, with one type P main component and no other losses. Consequently the only boundary types to be constructed for its compactified one-dimensional count are links of the legitimate instantons and those trace-minimum ends.
